`UnifiedActivationPipeline` in `.aios-core/development/scripts/unified-activation-pipeline.js` is the single entry point for ALL 12 agents; `generate-greeting.js` delegates to `UnifiedActivationPipeline.activate(agentId)`. `GreetingBuilder` assembles greetings; pipeline preloads enriched context. `loadUserProfile()` is called in `buildGreeting()` and passed to `_buildContextualGreeting()` to avoid double `resolveConfig()` calls. `GreetingPreferenceManager.getPreference(userProfile)` accepts optional userProfile for bob restriction; PM bypasses restriction. Bob non-PM: `auto` shows redirect; forced `named` shows simple named greeting.

Pipeline phases: 1 parallel 5 loaders (`Promise.all`); 2 agent definition; 3 sequential preference/session type/workflow; 4 enriched context; 5 GreetingBuilder. Eight agents use `visibility: [full, quick, key]`; `qa`, `data-engineer`, `devops`, `ux-design-expert` have NO visibility metadata and fall back to first 12 commands. `aios-master`: `visibility: full`. Bob mode returns empty commands for non-PM. `*yolo` is universal across all 12 agents. Badge: `_safeGetPermissionBadge()` in `greeting-builder.js`.

When mocking `resolveConfig`, use `mockReturnValue` (not `mockReturnValueOnce`) if called multiple times. `validate-user-profile.js` `validateUserProfile()` is pure (no filesystem). Always mock `fs`, `js-yaml`, `config-resolver`, and dependency modules BEFORE requiring the module under test. `resolveConfig()` merges L1-L5; L5 (`user-config.yaml`) has highest priority. `user_profile` is USER_FIELD in `migrate-config.js`; `toggleUserProfile()` in `config-resolver.js` flips bob<->advanced.

`PermissionMode` and `OperationGuard` in `.aios-core/core/permissions/` are fully functional. `cycleMode()` and `enforcePermission()` are wiring in `index.js`. Mode cycle: `explore`(0) -> `ask`(1) -> `auto`(2) -- `PermissionMode.MODE_CYCLE`.
